title: A Study of a Deterministic Networking Framework for Latency Critical Large Scientific Data Transfers
problem: Large data transfers in scientific workflows require deterministic completion-time guarantees. Traditional network scheduling lacks the deterministic latency bounds needed for deadline-sensitive scientific data transfers across backbone networks.
motivation: Scientific workflows increasingly depend on time-sensitive data transfers, requiring predictable completion times to meet application deadlines and optimize resource utilization.
method: The framework uses a scheduling method called Cyclic Queueing and Forwarding (CQF), which divides time into repeating cycles on network nodes that are synchronized to each other. It configures the length of these cycles so that any data packet starting at the beginning of a cycle will finish transferring to the next node before the cycle ends. The amount of data that can fit in each cycle depends on three things: how long the cycle is, how long it takes data to physically travel across the link, and how fast the link can send data. The system is tested by simulating it against two simpler approaches: one that always reserves a fixed amount of bandwidth, and another that reserves bandwidth dynamically as needed.
key_novelty: The key innovation is applying Cyclic Queueing and Forwarding to scientific data networks to guarantee data arrives by a specific deadline, potentially using multiple network paths to improve those guarantees.
contributions: CQF-based deterministic networking framework supporting large scientific data transfers with completion guarantees
Analysis of inter-node packet transfer capacity as a function of cycle time, propagation delay, and bandwidth
Empirical comparison demonstrating deterministic architecture achieves performance parity with dynamic bandwidth reservation while improving overall network utilization

metrics.other: completion-time guarantees comparable to dynamic bandwidth reservation, enhanced network bandwidth utilization

primary_theme: deterministic networking for scientific data transfers
